request.deadline: 18-month transition and operations period, with milestones from Q3 2026 through 2027
deliverables: Not-for-profit entity legally established or host-organization agreement signed under the preliminary board in Q3 2026.
Technical transition architecture and migration plan published for community review in Q3 2026.
Public usage dashboard made live in Q3 2026.
Board election held via on-chain voting under publicly published rules in Q4 2026.
All public API traffic for mainnet, preview, and preprod served by the new stack in Q1 2027.
Blockfrost source code, trademarks, domain names, and associated assets legally transferred to the governing entity in Q1 2027.
Public API operated at minimum 99% monthly uptime SLA during 2027 operational milestones.
Quarterly reports published covering technical metrics and budget summary.
request.what: Transition Blockfrost into a free, community-governed public good under an independent not-for-profit, including 18 months of transition and operations funding.

claims.claim: Blockfrost is described as a hosted REST interface that lets developers read from and interact with Cardano without running their own node.
The proposal says Blockfrost usage in the Cardano Foundation developer ecosystem survey rose from 39.3% in 2022 to 71.5% in 2025, with links to each survey year.
The proposal states that last month Blockfrost served 781k unique visitors, more than 1.84 billion API requests, almost 700 requests per second, and over 7 TB of API data.
The proposal states that in most Cardano epochs more than 50% of all transactions are submitted through Blockfrost.
The proposal states that more than 100 Icebreakers have joined the decentralized Blockfrost operator effort.
The proposal says 90% of all Cardano traffic served through the Blockfrost API comes from the free tier, making the commercial model difficult for financing the public-good operation.
The proposal commits to transferring all Blockfrost intellectual property, including source code, trademarks, domain names, and associated assets, to the governing not-for-profit entity.
The proposal requests 9,832,979 ADA, calculated from 1,868,266 USD at 0.19 USD per ADA, for 18 months of operations including the transition period.
The budget allocates 79.1% to staffing for a team of six plus overhead, 19.3% to operations and infrastructure, and 1.6% to legal and accounting.

The proposal states that long-term sustainability may come from not-for-profit paid tiers or a vendor-backed model, with future profits or fees supporting the public API and potentially returning commercial proceeds to the Cardano Treasury.

summary: The anchor describes a large treasury withdrawal to convert Blockfrost into a community-governed not-for-profit public API, with stated adoption metrics, governance milestones, IP-transfer commitments, service-level targets, and a budget dominated by staffing and infrastructure costs.
